The respondent No.1/Special Land Acquisition Officer, KIADB (Metro), Bengaluru, has made this reference under Sections 30 and 31 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (L.A. Act, 1894 for short) for apportionment of compensation amount.

.2. The brief facts of the case is that the respondent No.1 has acquired the land bearing Sy.No.20/5 measuring 94.37 sq. meters of Roopena Agrahara village, Begur Hobli,, Bengaluru South Taluka for the purpose of Metro Rail project.
As khathedars had not produced any title documents, the respondent has deposited the amount in the Court and deposited a sum of Rs.29,03,691/- after deducting 20% income tax.
The said L.A.C. No.57/2020 amount has been kept in F.D., in Bank of Baroda, Bannerghatta branch National Park Main Road, Bannerghatta, Bengaluru.
.3. After receipt of reference, this court has registered the case and issued notice to both parties.
In pursuance of service of notice, the claimant and respondents 1 and 2 entered appearance.

.4. The claimant G. Shashikala has filed claim statement, wherein, she admitted about issuance of Preliminary Notification and Final Notification, acquisition of land as claimed in the reference and also admitted that this reference has been made under Sections 30 and 31 of L.A. Act.
However, the claimant disputed that she has not approached the SLAO for payment of compensation claiming that produced documents and raised objections about the compensation determined by the SLAO.

She claimed that the market value of the acquired land is Rs. 63,803/- per Sq. Meters as per the compensation awarded to M/s. C.P. Developers but the compensation determined by the SLAO is much less.
L.A.C. No.57/2020

Further she claimed that subsequently an additional extent of 15 Sq. Meters is acquired by the respondents from the claimant in the same Sy. No.20/5 of Roopana Agrahara village and also stated about filing of W.P.No.6874/2021 before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.

The claimant further stated that her father B. Gopalappa was a tenant of said Sy. No. 20/5 to an extent of 22 guntas of land and the Land Tribunal granted occupancy rights with order dated 16.09.1981.

Subsequently the owner of the land challenged the said grant and the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka remanded the matter and subsequently the Land Tribunal vide order dated 01.04.1997 granted the occupancy rights in favour of claimant's father and the said order has attained finality.

The claimant's father Gopalappa executed the registered Will dated 15.04.2005 and thereby the claimant acquired the right, title and interest over the acquired property and claimant is the absolute owner of the acquired land and hence, she is entitled for compensation.
The respondent No.2 has filed objections stating that the land measuring 94.37 sq. meters in Sy.No.20/5 of Roopena Agrahara village came to be acquired for Bengaluru Metro Rail project.

The beneficiary of acquisition BMRCL sent compensation package of Rs.
45,43,825/- to the Special Land Acquisition Officer as per letter dated 07.01.2019 as notified khatedars did not show any interest in the matter.

Hence, the SLAO has passed the General Award on 22,02,2019 for a sum of Rs. 36,29,614/- inclusive of tax and referred the matter to the Civil Court under Sections 30 and 31 of L.A. Act for apportionment of compensation and deposited a sum of Rs.

He also deposited the deducted income tax of Rs.7,25,923/- through cheque No. 035495 dated 29.04.2019 in the Income Tax Department account at Corporation Bank, Race Course Road,
Khanija Bhavan, Bengaluru.

In view of the said deposit, the respondent No. 2 BMRCL who is beneficiary of acquisition will not be liable to pay interest L.A.C. No.57/2020 on the awarded compensation amount as held in the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in 1995(5) SCC 577 (SLAO Vs. Puttaiah and others, that the liability of the State to pay interest ceases with effect from the date of deposit.
.6. In order to prove their case, the GPA holder of claimant examined as PW.1.
The documents got marked at Exs.P.1 to 22.
The respondents' side not adduced oral evidence and got marked the documents.

.7. The following points that would arise for my consideration are:
"Whether the Claimant is entitle to receive compensation amount disputed in this case in- respect of property measuring 94.37 sq. meters in Sy.No.20/5 of Roopena Agrahara village?
.8.

Heard the arguments, perused the materials on record, my findings on the above point is in the affirmative, for the following:
L.A.C. No.57/2020 REASONS .9. POINT NO.1: This reference has been referred to the Court under Section 29 of the KIADB Act to decide the rightful recipient award amount deposited by the LAO.
As per Section 30 of the KIADB Act, 1966, the provisions of L.A. Act 1894 is applicable to the lands acquired under KIADB Act.
Section 30 of the L.A. Act speaks about dispute as to apportionment.

As per Section 30 of L.A. Act, when the amount of compensation has been settled under Section 11,
if any dispute arises as to the apportionment of the same or any part thereof, or as to the persons to whom the same or any party thereof is payable, the collector may refer such dispute to the decision of the Court.
.10. The present reference as stated earlier is under the ambit of Section 30 of the L.A. Act.
Therefore, the Court has to restrict its finding only to the extent that who is entitled for the compensation.
With this background the material placed before the Court has to be considered.

While making reference to the Court, the LAO / KIADB Metro Rail Project claimed that in spite of service of notice, the claimant has not come forward to execute the bond as contemplated under Section 29 (2) of KIADB Act.
Hence, SLAO referred this case to the Court.

Apart from that, there is no material before the Court that the claimant has moved any application before the SLAO for Shashikala G vs Slao Karnataka Industrial Area ... on 4 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187345334/
3 enhancement of compensation as required under law.

sentences.text: .12. Now the point to be considered is that whether the claimant proved her title over the acquired property.
The claimant in order to prove her title over the acquired property, examined her GPA holder / husband namely Basavaraju as PW.1 and also got marked Ex.P.1 to 22.
Ex.P.1 is the GPA executed by claimant in favour of PW.1.
Exs.P.2 to 4 are the certified copy of the order sheet / order by the Land Tribunal granting the occupancy rights, form No.10 / grant certificate and mutation order.

All these documents at Exs.P.2 to 4 shows that 22 guntas of L.A.C. No.57/2020 land in Sy.No. 20/5 of Roopena Agrahara village has been granted to the claimant's father B.
Gopalappa and accordingly the said property has been mutated in his name in the revenue records.
The grant of land in favour of claimant's father or acquisition of property by claimant's father is not in dispute.
.13. The claim of the claimant is that her father bequeathed the said property in her favour vide registered Will dated 15.04.2005.
Certified copy of the Will produced at Ex.P.7 and other documents such as Ex.P.8 and 9 shows that the property has been mutated in the name of claimant on the basis of the aforesaid registered Will.
Execution of Will and acquisition of property by the claimant from her father through Will is also not in dispute.
Therefore, nothing on record to disbelieve the title of claimant over the acquired property.
.14. The claimant also produced certified copy of the preliminary notification, notice and other documents.
As stated earlier, there is no dispute regarding the acquisition of property by issuing the notifications as well L.A.C. No.57/2020 as passing of the award.
Therefore, discussion of the said facts are not all required.

As stated earlier,
the only point to be the considered in this case is that whether claimant is entitled to receive the compensation.

The oral and documentary evidence produced by the claimant sufficiently shows that she is entitled to receive the compensation for the acquired land and the claimant is entitled to receive the compensation with statutory benefits.
Accordingly the above point is answered in affirmative.

In the result, the following:
 ORDER  The reference made by the and 31(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 is hereby allowed.

Claimant Smt. G. Shashikala is entitled to receive compensation in respect of Sy. No.
20/5 measuring 94.37 Sq. Meters of Roopena Agrahara village, Bangaluru South Taluka with statutory benefits.
